- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven resilience.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3-period average of forecast is > 80, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period; if < 70, increase by 1–3%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: forecast = 0.7×previous + 0.3×sentiment-adjusted trend.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model often misreads direction; use sentiment median over 3 days to anchor forecast instead of latest value.
